plain.text: Joseph had been taken to Egypt and bought by Potiphar. The LORD was with Joseph, and he prospered. Potiphar saw that the LORD gave him success in everything, so he put Joseph in charge of his whole household, and the LORD blessed the house because of Joseph. Joseph was well built and handsome, and Potiphar's wife wanted him to sleep with her. He refused: "My master has trusted me with everything. How could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?" She kept asking day after day. One day, when no one else was in the house, she caught him by his cloak. He left the cloak in her hand and ran out.

She called the household servants and accused Joseph of attacking her, showing his cloak as proof. She told her husband the same story. Potiphar was furious and put Joseph in the prison where the king's prisoners were held. But even there the LORD was with Joseph and showed him kindness, and gave him favour with the prison warden. The warden put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners. The LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.

summary.bigIdea: Joseph stays faithful when tempted and is falsely accused, but even in prison "the LORD was with Joseph".
points: Joseph does well in Potiphar's house because the LORD is with him.
He refuses to sin with Potiphar's wife and runs away.
Falsely accused and imprisoned, he is still blessed by God.
summary.reflection: Joseph did the right thing and still ended up in prison. How does the phrase "the LORD was with Joseph" speak to you?
